merger_description:
MJ Topco, LLC, a joint venture owned by MJWHP, LLC (together with its connected entities, **WHP Global**) and a subsidiary of G-III Apparel Group Ltd (together with its connected entities, **G-III**), proposes to acquire, through Majestic AcqCo, LLC, all of the issued and outstanding shares in Marc Jacobs Holdings, LLC (the **Target**) (the **Acquisition**).

WHP Global is US-headquartered. Globally, and in Australia, it acquires, manages and licences global consumer brands, and invests in high-growth distribution channels, including global expansion pathways and digital commerce platforms.

G-III similarly provides brand licensing and management services, in addition to the design, sourcing, distribution, marketing and retail supply of apparel, globally and in Australia.

The Target is a luxury fashion label founded by Marc Jacobs, headquartered in New York, USA, which offers high-fashion ready-to-wear apparel, handbags, cosmetics and fragrances. In Australia, its activities are limited to the wholesale and ecommerce sales of its apparel, handbags, cosmetics and fragrances.

determination_table_content.details:
MJ Topco, LLC, a joint venture owned by MJWHP, LLC (together with
its connected entities, WHP Global) and a subsidiary of G-III Apparel
Group Ltd (together with its connected entities, G-III), through
Majestic AcqCo, LLC, applied for a notification waiver in respect of
its proposed acquisition of 100% of the share capital in Marc Jacobs
Holdings, LLC (Marc Jacobs), as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

WHP Global is a US-headquartered brand management firm. It
acquires manages and licences global consumer brands. It invests in
high-growth distribution channels, including global expansion
pathways and digital commerce platforms. WHP Global owns the
intellectual property rights to a number of leading retail brands, of
which only the following are sold in Australia: Rag & Bone, Lotto, Tru,
and G-STAR.
WHP Global is indirectly controlled by Oaktree Capital Group, LLC
(Oaktree), which together with its affiliated investment funds and
other entities, comprises the ‘Oaktree group’. Oaktree is in turn jointly
controlled by Brookfield Asset Management Inc. (Brookfield).
Oaktree and Brookfield are global investment firms.
G-III provides brand licensing and management services, in addition
to the design, sourcing, distribution, marketing and retail supply of
apparel, globally and in Australia. G-III currently owns and licenses a
diverse portfolio of over 30 globally recognised fashion brands
including DKNY, Donna Karan and Karl Lagerfeld.
Marc Jacobs is a luxury fashion label headquartered in New York,
USA. It offers high-fashion ready-to-wear apparel, handbags, shoes,
cosmetics and fragrances. In Australia, its activities are limited to
the wholesale and online sales of its apparel, handbags, shoes,
cosmetics and fragrances.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between the parties in
the supply of brand licensing and management services
for consumer products, and in the manufacture,
distribution, and retail supply of luxury goods including
bags, small leather goods, apparel, footwear, cosmetics,
and fragrances in Australia
b. any increment in share of supply arising from the
Acquisition is estimated to be small
c. there are alternative providers of the relevant goods and
services, both in Australia and globally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
